newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Defense Dept delays health contract decision.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Defense Dept delays health contract decision.

text.p: The Defense Department has delayed a decision on the award of a five-year health services contract worth about $1.5 billion, and has asked both bidders for the contract to subimit a second "best and final offer," one of the bidding companies said on Monday.

Sierra Health Services Inc said its Baltimore-based subsidiary, Sierra Military Health Services Inc, had been notified that the selection of a contractor for a region of the Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Uniformed Services will be delayed until September 30. The selection was originally expected by May 1, the company said in a statement.
Sierra Health identified the second bidder for the contract as Foundation Health Systems Inc and said both companies had been asked to submit the second offers by July 21.
The contract encompasses 600,000 CHAMPUS beneficiaries in Washington, D.C. and 13 northeastern and mid-Atlantic states, Sierra Health said.
CHAMPUS beneficiaries include dependents of active duty military personnel, as well as retirees and their dependents, in all branches of the uniformed services.
